title: Rapido Product Strategy Case Study — by Swapnaneel Sarkar, Technical Product Manager
description: Rapido strategic case study by Swapnaneel Sarkar: FY25 revenue ₹934 Cr, 3.3M daily rides, the ₹9/day SaaS pivot, the bike-taxi legal battle, and four pre-IPO proposals — Two-Way Fare Pricing, Pro Captain Program, Priority Ride and Commuter Pass.

jsonld.headline: Rapido Strategic Case Study: India's Billion-Ride Platform — Disruptive Economics, Regulatory Navigation and the Multi-Modal Road to Profitability
jsonld.description: Strategic product analysis of Rapido with four pre-IPO proposals: Two-Way Fare Pricing, Pro Captain Program, Priority Ride and Commuter Pass.

html:
CASE STUDY · INDIAN URBAN MOBILITY · BY SWAPNANEEL SARKAR

Rapido Strategic Case Study — India's billion-ride platform

Disruptive economics, regulatory navigation, and the multi-modal road to profitability. A strategic product analysis by Swapnaneel Sarkar, Technical Product Manager at Heizen, Hyderabad. Open the full deck.

Context and traction

Rapido tripled its valuation from $1.1B (September 2024) to $3B within nine months on the back of primary and secondary rounds totalling $730M led by Prosus. FY25 operating revenue reached ₹934 Cr (+44%, total income above ₹1,000 Cr) while net losses narrowed 30% to ₹258 Cr. The platform completes 3.3M+ rides a day across 400+ cities, supported by more than 3M registered captains.

Origins and the core thesis: deliberately unglamorous

Founded in 2015 by IIT alumni Aravind Sanka, Pavan Guntupalli and Rishikesh SR to exploit India's two-wheeler density. While Ola and Uber chased premium ₹200+ car rides, Rapido cornered the hyper-frequent ₹40–80 urban commute, holding customer acquisition cost below ₹60 and building density in congested Tier 1, 2 and 3 cities.

Multi-modal product matrix

  • Core mobility — Rapido Bike & Auto: about 65% of national bike-taxi volume and roughly 25% of digital auto-rickshaw bookings.
  • Logistics — Rapido Box and the Magicpin partnership use rider capacity in non-commute gaps.
  • Ownly — a commission-free food-delivery pilot built on the captain network.
  • Integrations — metro and IRCTC ticketing inside the app for first- and last-mile journeys.

Business-model innovation: the SaaS pivot

In early 2024 Rapido replaced the traditional 25–30% commission with a flat software access fee of ₹9–29 per day, letting drivers keep 100% of the fare. The ₹9/day threshold attracted more than 2M monthly active drivers and pushed Uber and Ola into zero-commission subscription pilots of their own.

Audited financial performance

MetricFY22FY23FY24FY25
Operating revenue₹158 Cr₹443 Cr₹648 Cr₹934 Cr
YoY growth—~180%46%44%
Net lossn/a−₹675 Cr−₹371 Cr−₹258 Cr
Loss reduction YoY——45%30.5%
EBITDA margin———−19.59%

Source: Tofler registries and MCA audited filings, as compiled in the deck.

Gross order value grew from about $500M in FY24 to roughly $1.25B in FY25; Q2 FY25 bookings crossed ₹2,461 Cr (2.5× YoY) with 207M completed rides in the quarter and the quarterly net deficit down 77%.

Competition, governance and regulation

Uber's CEO named Rapido its principal competitor in India in mid-2025. Swiggy, a ~12% shareholder since 2022, exited to Prosus and WestBridge for ₹2,400 Cr (a 2.4× return) after the Ownly pilot created a conflict of interest, cleaning up the cap table ahead of an IPO. On the regulatory front, a decade-long battle over private two-wheeler permits ran from a 2015 launch in a legal vacuum, through the 2025 Karnataka High Court ban, to the January 2026 Division Bench ruling that bike-taxis are a legal passenger transport medium.

In August 2025 the Central Consumer Protection Authority fined Rapido ₹10 lakh over the "Auto in 5 min" campaign: guarantees compensated in Rapido coins rather than refunds, and nearly half of 1,224 National Consumer Helpline complaints unresolved. Support infrastructure must scale with bookings before an IPO prospectus.

Sustainability and expansion

Battery-swapping partnerships with Zypp Electric and Gogoro, HPCL fuel discounts, alignment with Delhi's EV Policy 2.0, and a target of 50% of the active fleet electric by 2027. Ownly challenges Swiggy and Zomato with zero restaurant commission, roughly 15% lower menu prices and a flat ₹30 consumer delivery fee, drawing on a 4M-captain pool.

Part II — four strategic solves to de-risk the pre-IPO roadmap

1. Two-Way Fare Pricing

In peripheries and mid-sized cities (~35% of rides) captains face 20–30 minute uncompensated dead-runs back to demand zones and start declining those trips. Proposal: route-level density modelling that predicts drop-off zones with low return-ride probability (under 30%), splits the dead-return cost between rider and platform, and explains the surcharge in-app. Target: 15–25% lower driver churn in low-density zones.

2. Pro Captain Program

A certified high-reliability tier: 200+ rides a month, rating above 4.7, biannual background checks, zero unresolved disputes. In return, guaranteed hourly floors, priority dispatch at peak, health-insurance top-ups, discounted EV leases, branded safety gear and NSDC-certified defensive-driving and service training. It doubles as a structural buffer against the CCPA compliance gap.

3. Priority Ride

An opt-in 15–25% premium for time-sensitive commuters instead of arbitrary surge: matched exclusively with Pro Captains, pickup guaranteed in under 7 minutes or the surcharge is refunded to the wallet. The premium funds the Pro Captain incentives.

4. Commuter Pass

A monthly pass piloted on high-density tech corridors with B2B trials, converting the most frequent riders into predictable recurring revenue.

Five-phase rollout

  • Phase 1 · Q3 2026 — pilot Two-Way Pricing; begin Pro Captain enrollment in Bengaluru. KPI: lower peripheral churn, higher acceptance.
  • Phase 2 · Q4 2026 — Pro Captains in the top 10 cities; support aligned with CCPA standards. KPI: 25% fewer complaints; 50,000+ verified Pro Captains.
  • Phase 3 · Q1–Q2 2027 — Priority Ride in 4 metros; Two-Way Pricing in 20 cities. KPI: priority bookings at 5% of metro volume, higher ARPU.
  • Phase 4 · Q3–Q4 2027 — Commuter Pass pilot and B2B trials. KPI: 10,000+ active pass holders, high NPS.
  • Phase 5 · FY28 — national rollout of premium tiers; IPO prospectus. KPI: sustainable premium revenue, predictable cash flows.

Risks: inconsistent state enforcement of two-wheeler permits (mitigated by designing passes and priority tiers to shift to auto and cab fleets) and incumbents' zero-commission pilots pressuring margins (mitigated by loyalty built on training, insurance and EV leases rather than commission alone).

Thesis

Supply economics first (fix route-level driver earnings), then quality verification (Pro Captain), then monetise reliability (Priority Ride, Commuter Pass). Affordable base services plus structured premium options give Rapido predictable cash flows and a credible profitability narrative ahead of its IPO.

title: HitWicket Product Analysis Case Study — by Swapnaneel Sarkar, Technical Product Manager
description: HitWicket case study by Swapnaneel Sarkar: a 60% day-1 drop-off diagnosed as a '15-minute exam' onboarding, and three bets — Challenger All-Stars, Rookie Rumble League and My Pro League — modelled at +25% D1 and +15% D7 retention.

jsonld.headline: Fixing the Funnel: Keep the Players — a retention strategy for Hitwicket Superstars
jsonld.description: Product analysis of HitWicket's onboarding drop-off with three engagement bets and a Q2–Q4 rollout plan.

html:
CASE STUDY · MOBILE SPORTS GAMING · BY SWAPNANEEL SARKAR

HitWicket case study — Fixing the funnel: keep the players

A breakdown of critical friction points, engagement engineering and retention loops for Hitwicket Superstars (mobile). Prepared by Swapnaneel Sarkar, Technical Product Manager at Heizen, Hyderabad. Open the full deck.

The core objective

Hitwicket has a rare gameplay engine driving 4.9 hours of average weekly play, but early onboarding leaks cap long-term viral growth. The first 15 minutes feel like an academic exam: dense nested menus, complex strategy definitions and multiple currencies before a player ever feels a crisp cover drive.

Metric deep-dive: 60% day-1 drop-off

Cohort analysis shows more than half of newly acquired players abandon the game during their first session, inflating customer acquisition cost and starving organic referral loops. Root cause: math-heavy screens, early menu blocks and no visual "wow" moment right after install.

Bet 1 — Challenger All-Stars

Let players play before teaching systems. Launch straight into a high-stakes scenario (10 runs off 3 balls, zero tutorial text), hand over a temporary max-level superstar squad to show the end-game fantasy, then transition to a rookie squad with a concrete unlock path. Visual action focus: dynamic cameras, predictive success overlays, one-touch batting and bowling inputs. Modelled impact: +25% day-1 retention and up to 35% fewer first-session uninstalls.

Bet 2 — Rookie Rumble League

A fair-match competitive sandbox for week one that prevents pay-to-win churn: normalised squad stats so stroke selection and bowler rotation decide matches, permanent profile badges and stadium cosmetics as stakes, and simulated opponents that keep waits under 15 seconds. Social sharing to Instagram and WhatsApp closes the loop. Modelled impact: +15% day-7 retention from fair play alone.

Bet 3 — My Pro League

Move players from casual sessions into daily habit loops with an automated weekly schedule: Mon–Tue T20 Quick Bash, Wed–Thu Super Over Decider, Fri–Sat Championship Round, Sunday All-Star Final, each with escalating rewards from XP boosts to exclusive skins. Target: 85% of active users inside automated daily loops, cutting reliance on remarketing.

Risks and mitigations

  • Simulated-opponent fatigue — introduce unpredictable tactical adjustments.
  • Ecosystem inflation — seasonal hard limits with conversion to cosmetics at cycle close.
  • UI overhead on low-end devices — progressive textures that scale to hardware profiles.

SWOT

Strengths: deep engagement (4.9h weekly), cult brand loyalty, unique strategy mechanics. Weaknesses: early drop-offs, interface overhead, heavy tutorials. Opportunities: IPL-season co-marketing, visual web hooks, localisation. Threats: well-funded casual titles, fast imitation, platform monetisation shifts.

Q2–Q4 rollout

  • Q2 · UX cleanse — re-engineer onboarding; prototype the Challenger All-Stars hook.
  • Q3 · Fair competition — ship the normalised Rookie Rumble sandbox and matchmaking.
  • Q3–Q4 · Habit loops — automated daily schedulers for My Pro League.
  • Q4 · Scaling — localised performance-marketing events.
